resources.string: Warn on top of games so you can save in time
Always on while the warning is on. It stays longer on the screen, because the console turns itself off soon after.

Android\'s own low battery notification is easy to miss during a full screen game. This shows a short banner across the top of the screen instead, once for each level while the console runs on battery. It doesn\'t take the buttons away from the game.\n\nThe console turns itself off when the battery is empty, and anything not saved is lost.
Battery %1$d %% - plug in a charger soon
Battery %1$d %% - save your game now. The console turns itself off soon.
Do Not Disturb and no pop-up notifications while you play
Turns on Do Not Disturb (priority only) and stops notifications from popping up over the game
On while a game or emulator is open, off when you leave it
Keeps the memory at full speed while you play, so its speed never changes in the middle of a game. Uses a little more battery.

When game mode ends, Do Not Disturb and pop-up notifications go back to how they were. If you change Do Not Disturb yourself in the meantime, your change stays.

An app counts as a game if it says it is one, or if it is one of the common emulators such as RetroArch or PPSSPP.

The performance profile you had comes back too, unless you picked another one while playing.

What Do Not Disturb lets through is set in Settings > Sound > Do Not Disturb.
Open it again after a restart
If a game was open when the console turned off, also when the battery ran out, it opens again about 10 seconds after the home screen

Continue brings back the last game you played, in one press: the Continue tile in Quick Settings, FN + A, or the power menu.

A game that is still open comes back just where you left it. Otherwise RetroArch and PPSSPP start the same game again, RetroArch with the same core; other games just open again.

You go on from the game's own last save. RetroArch writes it every 10 seconds when it changes. Save states are never loaded or written for you: if your newest save state is newer than the game's own save, a message tells you.
Can\'t find the game file of %1$s. Is the SD card in?
RetroArch\'s core for %1$s isn\'t installed any more
Continuing %1$s. Your newest save state (%2$s) is newer than the game\'s own save. To use it, load it in the RetroArch menu (Select + X).
Remember a manual brightness choice for each app

Choose apps below. Their brightness is used only in manual mode. Leaving them restores the previous brightness unless you changed the slider yourself. A slider change pauses rules until you leave the configured apps.\n\nApps that control their own window brightness are skipped. The check runs when the task changes; later window-only changes may be seen on the next task change. If the window brightness check is unavailable, the rule is skipped. Rules stop on the subsystem launch screen and while the guest owns the session.
Choose repairs, preview changes and keep a backup

Choose the repairs to apply below. All are selected to start; turn off any you want to keep as they are. Saves, bindings and library entries are kept. Per-game overrides are left intact and may still enable these features. An FPS increase is not guaranteed. Exit RetroArch before continuing.
Removes screen effects such as scanlines from the main settings to reduce graphics work. Games lose those effects unless an override enables them.
Stops extra frame processing in the main settings to reduce processor work. Controls may feel less immediate because this optional input-delay reduction is disabled.

Turns off shaders and Preemptive Frames in the existing Game Boy / Game Boy Color core settings. This reduces graphics and processor work, at the cost of screen effects and optional input-delay reduction. A missing override stays missing.

Turns off shaders and Preemptive Frames in the existing Nestopia NES core settings. This reduces graphics and processor work, at the cost of screen effects and optional input-delay reduction. A missing override stays missing.

Turns off shaders and Preemptive Frames in the existing FCEUmm NES core settings. This reduces graphics and processor work, at the cost of screen effects and optional input-delay reduction. A missing override stays missing.

%1$d configuration files would change.

Selected repairs:
%2$s

Only these repairs will be applied. Core overrides can take priority over global settings. A backup of changed files is saved before applying. Per-game overrides are kept. Custom override directories are not supported.
Restore the files saved before the repair. Restore is refused if those files were edited afterward. Exit RetroArch first.
Waiting for the setup worker… Keep RetroArch closed.
Preview ready. Cancel leaves your settings unchanged.
Selected repairs applied. The backup is available through Restore backup.
The selected repairs need no changes. Any existing backup was kept.
RetroArch is running. Exit it normally and try again.
A backup already exists. Restore it before making another repair.

Unable to complete the request. Check that RetroArch has a global configuration, uses the default override directory and is closed. Restore also requires an existing backup and unchanged repaired files. Any backup made before a failed write is kept for recovery.
The setup worker has not answered yet. The request may still be queued; keep RetroArch closed and check again later.
